description: Adaptation Tool Kit: Sea-Level Rise and Coastal Land Use is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Georgetown Climate Center; Georgtown University Law Center | Harrison Institute for Public Law. This report describes how local governments can use land-use practices to adapt to sea-level rise. It helps policymakers manage the complexity of adaptation by identifying and organizing adaptation tools. In this case, the tools are generally used legal devices such as laws and policies. The Tool Kit describes each potential tool by:. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Flooding – Coastal, Flooding – General, Landslides. Assets: Natural Areas and Wildlife, Property. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
